title: Deep learning diagnoses influenza from pharyngeal images and clinical information
summary: A deep-learning model using pharyngeal images and clinical information predicted PCR-confirmed influenza, with validation AUC 0.90, sensitivity 76% and specificity 88% in 659 patients (196 with influenza) across 11 hospitals in January-March 2020, outperforming three physicians. Heat maps focused on posterior pharyngeal follicles. Data are from Japan only, sensitivity is 76% and a specialized camera is required.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model on pharyngeal images plus clinical information to diagnose PCR-confirmed influenza
organization: Aillis, Inc; Japanese Red Cross Medical Center

evidence.tested: Separate validation stage in 659 patients (196 with influenza) at 11 hospitals in a later period, against PCR, with a three-physician comparison.
evidence.unknown: Performance outside Japan; physician comparison details; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning model predicted PCR-confirmed influenza from throat images and clinical data.
